answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to laser spectroscopy of natural shale. Each node pulses an optical beam at its mineral sample to ignite a plasma plume, transmitting the resulting emission spectrum as proof. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of maintaining dedicated physical spectrometers and unique geological targets per identity. However, ambient air currents like a stray zephyr can disrupt plume expansion, occasionally rejecting valid nodes.
